answer: Shared-cost escrow pool.** Each identity pays a fixed deposit into a common vault before its first action; deposits are released only after the identity's work is verified by unrelated peers. When duplicate or coordinated identities appear, the pool pays the verification cost from their deposits rather than from honest members. An attacker must fund every sock puppet up front and forfeit deposits on detection, so the per-identity cost scales with the tide of fake accounts rather than the ocean of honest ones.
